conversation:
Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm 39 years old, and I'm here because my right upper arm has been hurting really badly. It happened when I was playing volleyball, and someone kicked my legs out from under me, causing me to fall on my arm. The pain is severe, like a nine out of 10.
Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the injury to your right upper arm in more detail, including when it occurred and any immediate treatment you received?
Patient: I'm 39 years old, and I'm female. The injury happened when I was playing volleyball last night around 7 o'clock. Someone from the other team kicked my legs out from under me as I was spiking the ball, and I fell on my right arm, right on my shoulder. It was really nasty, and the pain has been severe ever since. I've been taking ibuprofen every six hours, but it's not helping much.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, bruising, deformity, or loss of function in your right upper arm since the injury? Additionally, are you experiencing any numbness or tingling in your arm or hand?
Patient: There's some swelling and redness on my right shoulder, and it's tender to touch. I can straighten my elbow, but I can't move my shoulder without pain. I don't have any numbness or tingling in my arm or hand.
Doctor: Have you experienced any previous shoulder injuries or conditions that might affect this current injury?
Patient: No, I haven't had any previous shoulder injuries, but I did have a lumbar fusion surgery about six years ago. Other than that, I have gallstones and take Pepcid for it.
Doctor: Could you please describe any recent symptoms related to your lumbar fusion surgery or gallstones that might be relevant to your current condition?
Patient: I don't have any recent symptoms related to my lumbar fusion or gallstones. The only issue I've had lately is the pain in my right upper arm after the volleyball injury. My gallstones haven't caused any problems recently, and I just take Pepcid as needed.
Doctor: Could you please describe the range of motion of your right shoulder, including any specific movements that cause pain or are limited? Additionally, have you noticed any deformity, instability, or clicking in the shoulder joint?
Patient: I can straighten my elbow, but I can't move my shoulder without pain. I don't notice any deformity or instability, and there's no clicking in the joint. It's just really tender and swollen on the shoulder area.
Doctor: Have you had any imaging studies, such as X-rays or an MRI, of the right shoulder since the injury occurred?
Patient: No, I haven't had any imaging studies of my right shoulder since the injury. The doctor just showed me the X-ray during our conversation, and it showed a fracture in my humerus. I was told it looks like the top of a snow cone got knocked off.
